item.title: Israeli opposition urges voters to turn out to end Netanyahu’s rule
item.description: Israeli opposition leaders on Tuesday urged voters to turn out in large numbers in the country’s parliamentary elections to end Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s rule, Anadolu reports. Voting began at 7 am local time (0500GMT) and is scheduled to continue until 10 pm (2000GMT). Opposition Yisrael Beiteinu party leader and former Defense Minister Avigdor Lieberman called on Israelis to vote to bring an end to Netanyahu’s political era. “Vote. Let’s put an end to the Netanyahu era and the rule of the Haredim,” Lieberman wrote on US social media company X, referring to ultra-Orthodox religious groups. item.title: Netanyahu’s Likud plans to film Arab voters outside Israel’s polling stations: Report
item.description: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s Likud party plans to deploy teams to film Arab voters outside polling stations during Tuesday’s general elections, potentially using the footage to support claims of electoral fraud if the party suffers major losses, Haaretz daily reported. The newspaper said Likud has spent millions of shekels recruiting and paying workers to monitor polling stations in Arab communities, record voters and report developments to party headquarters in real time. The teams, established in recent weeks, will operate outside polling stations rather than inside them, allowing them to avoid the strict regulations governing official election observers. item.title: Netanyahu warns 'left-wing women are escorting Arab women to the polls'
item.description:
Netanyahu warns 'left-wing women are escorting Arab women to the polls'

Benjamin Netanyahu has warned his supporters that "left-wing women are escorting Arab women to the polls."

According to Haaretz, the prime minister sent voters a recorded message, accusing leftists and Palestinian-led parties of trying to "steal the election."

He added that police had "caught three senior [Ra'am] officials with envelopes of cash in the south."

item.title: Kuwait sentences three to death over plot to assassinate interior minister, alleged links to Iran and Hezbollah
item.description: A Kuwaiti court has sentenced three individuals to death and eight others to five years in prison in a case involving an alleged plot to assassinate Interior Minister Sheikh Fahad Al-Yousef and accusations of collusion with Iran and the Lebanese group Hezbollah. The verdict was issued by Kuwait’s State Security and Terrorism Crimes Court, presided over by Judge Nasser Al-Bader, alongside judges Omar Al-Mulaifi, Abdullah Al-Faleh and Salem Al-Zayed. According to the prosecution, the defendants faced charges of collaborating with foreign entities, planning hostile acts against Kuwait, targeting senior government officials, joining a banned organization and engaging in activities deemed harmful to national interests. item.title: Election committee says no evidence of ballot tampering despite complaints from at least six parties
item.description:
Election committee says no evidence of ballot tampering despite complaints from at least six parties

Israel's Central Elections Committee (CEC) has said there is no evidence of systemic tampering with ballots in the election, despite complaints from at least six opposition parties.

The Times of Israel said that Yashar, B’Yachad, People of Israel, Yisrael Beytenu, Ra’am, and the Reservists-Economic party had all reported alleged irregularities, including "missing or defaced ballot slips and other suspected attempts to interfere with voting."

Yashar said they had raised a complaint after suspicions that reports of irregularities were not "isolated mishaps."

“The large number of incidents raises serious suspicions that these are not isolated mishaps, but rather a systematic and deliberate attempt to sabotage the democratic process, prevent citizens from exercising their right to vote and influence the election results,” they said in a statement.

item.title: Israel rejects UN commission’s findings on genocide and crimes against humanity as “political propaganda”
item.description: Israel on Monday rejected the findings of a UN-mandated investigative commission accusing it of committing crimes against humanity, including extermination, against Palestinians in the occupied West Bank and continuing to commit genocide in the Gaza Strip. In a statement, the Israeli Ministry of Foreign Affairs dismissed the commission’s report as “political propaganda,” rejecting its conclusions concerning Israeli actions in the Palestinian territories. “This is not a human rights report, but a document of political propaganda detached from reality,” the ministry said. It accused the commission of seeking to “undermine Israel’s right to self-defence, delegitimise the Jewish state, and legitimise jihadist terrorism against its citizens.” The Israeli response followed the commission’s findings concerning violations against Palestinians in the occupied West Bank […]

item.title: Palestinians are voting in Israel to ensure their very survival
item.description:
Palestinians are voting in Israel to ensure their very survival

Ibrahim Said has boycotted Israeli elections since voting in 1980.

Parties came and went, telling him they would defend his interests if elected, even promising to help return his lands in al-Birwa, the town his family were displaced from during the 1948 Nakba.

But nothing ever changed for the better for Palestinian citizens of Israel. Israeli democracy had nothing to offer him and his community, the 70-year-old felt.

This year, the situation is completely different.

“Without a doubt, we must vote this time. We are living in fear,” Said tells Middle East Eye in his garage in the Galilee.

Read more: Palestinians are voting in Israel to ensure their very survival
